lines.text: September 2nd, 2026. Anthropic publishes an open-source blueprint for commerce agents. Shopify ships an implementation — the same day. This — is Shopware's.
This is not a Claude shop. It's Shopware as the commerce execution layer — the system any agent runs on.
Two agents ship in the box. A shopping agent — search, compare, build a real cart, hand off to Shopware checkout. And a merchant agent — analyze, stage a change, a human approves — then it's applied.

Here's the wiring. Anthropic's blueprint packages — pinned, unmodified. Two thin Shopware backends. Shoppers go through UCP — discovery, then MCP. Merchants go through the Admin API and MCP — with dry-run previews computed on the server.
One curl to the well-known endpoint, and Shopware announces what it speaks — catalog, cart, checkout, order, identity linking — and the keys it signs with.

Three things Shopware brings that a bolt-on can't. Native UCP — discovery, signatures, identity linking. Dry-run previews — straight from the core. And commerce semantics where they belong — promotions, rules, variants, price disclosures.

The rules are enforced, not prompted. The model proposes. A person — or a policy — applies. Provenance gates accept only IDs the session has seen. And checkout completes in Shopware — never in the agent.
Watch it run. Search the live catalog. Add to a real Shopware cart. Then — Check out on Shopware. Same cart, same total — in the shop's own checkout.
On the merchant side — a price change is staged. Before and after, previewed by the server. Nothing touches the shop until someone approves. Then one call applies it.
Shopware is the Commerce Operating System for the Agent Economy. The repo is shopware slash claude-commerce-agents. Five commands — and it runs.
